title: Class-prior / base-rate correction of the adapted OOD score
why: O4 adapted score (AUROC 0.781) is an uncalibrated z-score; P1 (#137) showed its calibrated 0.5-band collapses. Test whether prior/base-rate correction can rescue a non-collapsing band.
hypothesis: A 0.5-band on the calibrated adapted score collapses at the 13.75% OOD bad rate; prior correction cannot fix it.
data: 160 human-labelled Egocentric-10K windows (138 good / 22 bad, 47 factories); O4 adapted score (stable-8 + Z3-6); IndEgo 150-window gold
method: leave-factory-out Platt + IndEgo-source prior-shift (logit offset) calibration; symmetric 0.5-band sweep w=0..0.30
summary: LFO Platt max P(bad)=0.60, 0/22 bad rejected at 0.5, full-decision BA 0.496; prior-shifted (logit offset -1.143) max P(bad)=0.579, still 0/22 rejected. Base-rate correction pushes the posterior toward GOOD (OOD bad rarer than IndEgo), so the 0.5-band collapses further. The frontier must be a rank/quantile rule, not a probability band.
decision: Drop the 0.5-probability band on the adapted score; use a prior-free rank/quantile threshold (N2.02).

title: Prior-free rank/quantile operating frontier on the adapted OOD score
why: Turn the adapted score's OOD AUROC 0.781 into a non-collapsing review-vs-error frontier that beats the frozen O3 frontier (44.2% review, BA 0.708).
hypothesis: A deterministic within-regime quantile rule on the adapted score lowers OOD error at any review budget <=60%.
data: 160 OOD labels (22 bad, 47 factories); 1,546 unlabelled E8 windows (review workload, exact by construction)
method: global (within-regime) quantile reject-lowest-q / accept-highest-q / review-middle; within-factory quantile; asymmetric 2-D sweep; factory-grouped 2000x bootstrap BA CI
summary: Adapted(b) global quantile: q=0.28 -> 44.0% review, BA 0.793 [0.686,0.891]; q=0.30 -> 40.0%, BA 0.751 [0.584,0.879]; q=0.20 -> 60.0%, BA 0.808 [0.683,0.911]. Asymmetric accept 25%/reject 15% -> 60.0%, BA 0.857 [0.746,0.939]. 3 points strictly dominate the frozen 0.708@44.2% (lower review AND higher BA). Within-factory rule is deployable (17-119 windows/factory on 1,546) but not validatable on the 160 (1-4 windows/factory, BA~chance).
decision: Adopt the global-quantile rule q=0.28 (44% review, BA 0.793) as the adapted operating point; symmetric q=0.20 (60%, 0.808) if a 60% budget is preferred.

title: Split conformal on the adapted score + joint review-vs-error frontier
why: Give the adapted-score frontier a distribution-free coverage guarantee and place every method on one joint table vs the frozen O3 reference.
hypothesis: Leave-factory-out split conformal on the adapted score has honest marginal coverage and the same (dominant) frontier.
data: 160 OOD labels (22 bad, 47 factories); 1,546 unlabelled E8 windows
method: split/LAC conformal, leave-one-factory-out (score_good=s, score_bad=-s); coverage on held-out factories; joint frontier table with false-accept/false-reject
summary: Conformal empirical coverage tracks nominal on held-out factories (0.95->0.944, 0.85->0.850, 0.70->0.700, 0.65->0.650). REVIEW is U-shaped, min ~4.4% (on 160) at nominal 0.65 (q crosses 0), BA 0.728. Best <=60% review point: asymmetric accept25/reject15 -> 60.0%, BA 0.857 [0.746,0.939]; symmetric q=0.20 -> 60.0%, BA 0.808. Beats frozen 0.708@44.2% on both axes (3 dominating points). Paired grouped BA diff q=0.28 vs frozen w=0.16 = +0.092 [-0.053,0.281], 87.3% >0. Caveats: transductive quantile, test-set-selected argmax, n_bad=22, fixed-threshold 1546 review% not computable (not cached).
decision: Ship the adapted quantile frontier; the joint improvement is real and driven by ranking (AUROC 0.781 vs 0.566), not calibration.
